quote: Gate A: ≥ 10× better than the SAD floor (...) on held-out-chemistry Defect Set splits, target ≤ 0.5% normalized MAE. (...) Any gate failed after the full budget (both samplers tried) kills the task
assessment: Only a weak reading covers this: the canon's kill condition is the 10x ratio, and 'target <= 0.5%' can be read as a goal rather than a bar (the floor measures 0.154, so 10x gives 0.0154 and 0.5% would be about 31x); no document (IMPLEMENTATION.md lines 50-54 say only 'a factor of ten', report.md, operator-results.md, commits) records why the target was dropped from the ladder, and the member has not trained, so no result exists.

quote: POTCAR files are license-restricted: contents are never quoted, and POTCAR-derived artifacts never leave `/Pool`.
assessment: Only a weak reading covers this: the title is the identifier VASP echoes into OUTCAR (commit 4e2f24f: 'it is assumed already resolved by whatever reads the OUTCAR TITEL echo, and no POTCAR is opened, quoted, or referenced'), so it can be read as metadata rather than licensed contents; but no repository document says titles are exempt, the title is literally the POTCAR header line, deep_dft/IMPLEMENTATION.md also quotes one, and /Pool/VASP_DATA/read-me-first.md item 8 describes the remote as public, so the excuse does not settle the claim.

Nothing excuses this. I searched report.md, IMPLEMENTATION.md, report.py comments (Grid_Shift_Probe_Set), operator-results.md and every commit touching operators/alias_free_convolutional/. None records why 21 synthetic resamplings of evaluation-block runs replace the census's 21 real axis-stretched D2 cells (ANSWERS.md D2-4: 'only the 21 axis-stretched anisotropic cells deviate (72–84 per axis)'). The canon's own 'sinc-resampled inputs' only half supports the substitution, and the cited phrase names real cells, so the claim stands. Nothing has trained.

quote: There is **no fine-grid ELF ground truth anywhere**, so super-resolved ELF output is a self-consistency check only, never a headline.
assessment: Only a partial reading covers this: the grid-shift bar compares the CNO's error inflation with the twin's against the same resampled target, so it can be read as a relative self-consistency check, which the canon allows, rather than a headline ELF accuracy; but the bar decides an entry rejection, the targets on 76-84 axes are partly super-resolved, and no document records the choice or its limits.

quote: **Build (the entry's identity).** The **fused activation-resampling kernel (act2x) with a custom VJP** (...) alias-free surcharge ≈ +40% kernel effort over a plain U-Net.
assessment: Only a partial reading covers this: the canon names act2x as the entry's identity and the cost the surcharge prices, so a twin that differs only in the activation does isolate that piece; but the canon's comparator is a 'plain U-Net', the twin keeps sinc resampling (multi_scale.py Downsampled_By_Two/Upsampled_By_Two through Spectral_Resampled), and IMPLEMENTATION.md calls it 'the canon's own' comparator without recording the difference (report.md only says 'stand-in').

quote: CNO must match-or-beat a width-matched plain U-Net at native grids **and** degrade at most half as much under grid-shift probes (the 21 axis-stretched 72–84 cells; sinc-resampled inputs).
assessment: Only a partial reading covers this: the canon itself asks for native-grid operation and a grid-shift probe that measures degradation, and on the real stretched cells the grid length grows with the cell length, so whole-voxel stencils keep roughly fixed physical support; that does not hold for the member's synthetic resamplings of one cell, and IMPLEMENTATION.md ('Combined_Coarse_Input is called with target_shape set to the input's own native shape ... this member has no truncate-early step') describes native processing without giving a reason.

quote: **Three scales, not four.** A fourth halving breaks on the 84-axis stretched probe cells (84 → 42 → 21 → 10.5), and the grid-shift probe is load-bearing evidence this entry needs (...) Reported here rather than silently widened to chase the estimate — widening the channel sequence is a one-line change (`hidden_channel_widths=`) if the team wants to spend more capacity, but that is a call for whoever owns the pre-registered configuration
assessment: The excuse covers part of the claim: IMPLEMENTATION.md gives a reason for dropping the fourth (256-wide) scale and reports the 488,034 count openly, so the cut is not hidden; but it measures the count against a '1–2M build brief' that no repository document holds and never states the canon's ≈9M, so the size of the cut against the test plan goes unrecorded (written in commit 9cd3b34, before any training).

Nothing excuses this. I searched test-suite.md, operator-results.md, both member documents and the member's commits for '12 h', '8 h', 'cap', 'wall-clock', 'budget' and '500 epochs'. The caps appear only as plan text ('cap 8 h', 'cap 12 h') with no reason against the canon's 500 epochs (about 1–2.5 days). A possible mitigation, also unrecorded: the canon's epoch-time estimate assumed the ≈9M model, not the 488k one. Neither run has trained.

quote: the ridge fits density, gradient magnitude and Laplacian pointwise against the same remainder the climatology averages, trained on the same runs; it is coordinate-blind where the climatology is a positional template over near-identical defect geometries, so it only edges past Hartree + climatology, and this combination is now the canonical rho-to-V floor every entry cites
assessment: Partial: stage0-report.md (commit 1de8057, 2026-09-11, before the 2026-09-12 potential floors in 6808286) records that the ridge replaces the climatology and why (it edged past it on the defect-only spin-mean block), and test-suite.md I.1 names the bar as the 'spectral-Poisson + semilocal-XC floor'; but the stated reason fails on the block actually used: factorized_fourier/report.md and operator-results.md print Hartree + climatology at 40.3% against the ridge's 47.96% and still anchor on the weaker one, and no document records why, so the looser 23.98% bar is not excused.

I searched every 'climatolog' mention in test-suite.md, operator-results.md, stage0-report.md, the factorized_fourier docs and code, operators/evaluation/localization_block.py (Climatology_Fields and Potential_Floor_Rows average over block.floor_train with no campaign split) and the commit history of localization_block.py: nothing records pooling the template across the two cubic campaigns against test-suite.md 9.6's 'per-campaign climatology', and the stage-zero version was defect-only, so it was per-campaign by construction.

quote: The defect rows, not the pooled median, are this member's real test.
assessment: Partial: report.md (written with the result in 42f67eb) prints the defect-set floors and member rows and calls the defect rows the real test, so the canon's held-out Defect Set population can be read off it and the verdict holds there (0.002329 vs 0.049247); but the pre-registered ladder and the results page still state the kill on the pooled block and print an em dash for defect-set floors that report.md measured, and no document records why the population changed.

quote: Two kill floors, both scored at the level's own mean field over whatever functional variants share it ... (`Build_Field_Cache` pools both functionals ...) ... a seventh branch feature (0.0 cheap, 1.0 accurate, both functionals pooled in one training set)
assessment: Partial: IMPLEMENTATION.md (6860366, written before training) openly states that the floors and the training pool both functionals, and test-suite.md line 127 allows functional identity as a conditioning input; but it gives no reason for scoring against a PBE/HSE mean field that is neither functional's target, and nothing records the missing per-functional rows the never-pool rule requires ('metrics are reported per campaign and per functional, always'), nor the same construction in factorized_fourier's Cached_Level_Field.

I searched test-suite.md II.1 and 9.2, deep_operator_network/IMPLEMENTATION.md and report.md, and the commit (f205acd) that wrote the page sentence: II.1(b) names the extrapolation split ('hold out all factor-0.8 runs, separately 1.2'), and 9.2's 'Perovskite - 5-fold + the extrapolation variant' does not make fold 0 the judged block; the member's own report.md scores the holdout rows with 'kill' verdicts, so nothing supports the page's 'the canon judges fold 0 ... not kills'.

I searched residual_correction/IMPLEMENTATION.md, report.md, report.py, every commit message touching operators/residual_correction/, and every use of card.loss or delta_mean_squared_error in the package: the card names delta_mean_squared_error (per-pair MSE over the pair's identity MSE, operators/metrics Delta_Mean_Squared_Error), the trainer's Correction_Loss is plain correction MSE, and no document records the change. The only partial reading is that canon IV.1's whole-block delta-R-squared has a constant denominator, so plain MSE matches it, but that does not reconcile the card's per-pair weighting.

I searched deep_dft/report.md, IMPLEMENTATION.md, the deep_dft code and the history of deep_dft and operators/tasks/__init__.py: the structure_to_charge_defects and _alloy cards carry only pseudopotential_titles as a covariate, the report's floors and gates are pooled over both functionals, and nothing records why the never-pool rule's per-functional reporting is dropped (the member is untrained, so no result is affected yet).

quote: fold 0 (evaluation) 76 runs, fold 1 (validation) 65 runs, folds 2-4 (member training) 196 runs pooled, folds 1-4 pooled (floor and basis training) 261 runs ... `Fitted_Bases` fits both proper-orthogonal bases (`operators.data.Gram_Pod`, rank 32) on the pooled 261 floor-training snapshots and reports the reconstruction-error decay ... the POD gate the canon names.
assessment: Partial: IMPLEMENTATION.md (1649dca, before training; the coefficient statistics were added in 20ef323, also before the v2 result) records that the bases and statistics are fit on folds 1-4 and ties that to the stage-zero POD gate population; fold 0 stays untouched, so the canon's stated purpose (no test leakage) holds. But no document gives a reason for letting the member's own early-stopping fold into its input statistics, nor notes that factorized_fourier and alias_free_convolutional fit theirs on folds 2-4, so the results page calling these 'training-fold statistics' goes unexplained.
